items.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: we would go on the road for four, six weeks at a time and the New York bands had two bands. We would alternate with Sonny Rollins, alternate with

ctx.x: ’45 to ’65, I was really in love with the mid-60s and Cannonball Adderley in particular. I loved the combination of his bebop influence but then what we called “soul jazz” I guess, and him in particular. Did you ever play with him?

No, no. Never ever. “Cleanhead” would always refer to him. “I know that little fat boy.” And he talked about John Coltrane. “That little boy played in my band.” You know. So “Cleanhead” was in, and I was playing with “Cleanhead” when he went to New York and he made a record with Cannonball. I was playing with him as a kid, then. That had to be the late 50s. So yeah. But Cannonball, there was a fad, and that was the period, there’s two particular styles that made the music flourish: the bossa nova and the soul to…
different people They’d play an hour, we’d play an hour. This was going, there’d be six sets.
